title: Variance Stress Comparison: v3.1 vs v3.0 vs v2.9 - November 2026
content:
Summary:

This doc summarizes the variance & stress comparison run we performed on three candidate inference model builds (v2.9, v3.0, v3.1) across 6 prompt families. The goal was to measure win/loss on task accuracy, hallucination rate, calibration, latency (p50/p95), and token-cost to inform a safe canary rollout strategy for v3.1.

Quick verdict (TL;DR):
- v3.1 is a clear quality uplift on open-ended synthesis and instruction-following (net win-rate ~62% vs v3.0), with meaningful reductions in hallucination for retrieval-augmented prompts.
- v3.1 shows regressions on structured numerical/math tasks (win-rate ~38% vs v3.0) and slightly higher p95 latency (+12–18ms) on 8k contexts when using fused attention kernels.
- Recommendation: proceed with a conservative canary of v3.1 for hosted + dedicated low-traffic routes for 2 weeks, with auto-fallback to v3.0 on error/latency SLO breach and a hard block on math-heavy routes until patch PR #459 lands.

Experimental setup (notes):
- Workload: 12k examples across 6 prompt families: instruction (2k), summarization (2k), code-assist (2k), math/structured (2k), RAG QA (2k), safety/toxicity probes (2k).
- Splits: 80/20 heldout for significance testing; each example scored by both automated metrics and sampled human raters (n=3) for subjective quality where applicable.
- Hardware: Dedicated A100 cluster (4x A100 nodes), identical runtime kernel selection; quantization: int8 for v3.0 & v3.1, v2.9 baseline uses fp16.
- Inference config: temperature=0.0/0.3 for deterministic vs generative lanes, max_tokens=512, streaming disabled for latency numbers.
- Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap for win-rate CIs, McNemar for paired binary outcomes on correctness.

Leaderboards (aggregated):
- Overall human-preference win-rate (pairwise, higher is better): v3.1 vs v3.0: 62% (95% CI: 58–66%), v3.0 vs v2.9: 55% (95% CI: 51–59%).
- Automated task accuracy (micro-avg across tasks): v3.1 83.2%, v3.0 79.6%, v2.9 74.1%.
- Hallucination rate (lower is better, measured on RAG QA subset): v3.1 4.8%, v3.0 7.9%, v2.9 12.3%.
- Safety flags triggered (toxicity probes, higher is worse): v3.1 0.7% flagged, v3.0 0.6% flagged — difference not significant (p>0.1).

Latency / cost summary (per 1 request, 2k context median workload):
- p50 latency: v3.1 48ms, v3.0 44ms, v2.9 60ms.
- p95 latency: v3.1 142ms, v3.0 128ms, v2.9 210ms.
- Estimated token cost (normalized units): v3.1 1.02x, v3.0 1.00x, v2.9 1.18x.
- Note: higher p95 for v3.1 correlates with fused-kernel codepath under contention; root cause annotated in PR#462.

Task breakdown (selected highlights):
1) Instruction-following / assistant behavior:
- v3.1 shows better context utilization, fewer irrelevant digressions. Human preference 68% over v3.0.
- Edge case: long chains of multi-step instructions occasionally truncate steps when temperature=0.0. TODO: add prefix-preserve caching test.

2) Summarization (long documents):
- v3.1 achieves higher ROUGE-L and better factuality in RAG settings. Hallucination reduction most pronounced when retrieval returned high-precision snippets.

3) Code-assist (synthesis & edits):
- v3.1 and v3.0 parity on simple code generation. v3.1 improves edit suggestion quality for multi-file refactor prompts (win-rate 59%).
- Failure modes: v3.1 sometimes over-suggests API changes not present in the prompt; created 6/200 regression tickets labeled "spec-drift".

4) Math / structured reasoning (red flag):
- v3.1 underperformed v3.0 on arithmetic and constrained-output tasks (win-rate 38%). Error pattern suggests loss of learned symbolic heuristics after recent training curriculum tweak.
- Severity: medium — impacts product routes that rely on numeric precision (billing summaries, analytics copilot).

5) Retrieval-augmented QA (RAG):
- v3.1 > v3.0 in quote-anchored answers and citation placement. Hallucination down from 7.9% to 4.8%.

6) Safety & toxicity probes:
- No meaningful regressions. Run includes OASST-derived adversarial list; v3.1 did not surface new high-severity safety issues.

Win/Loss table (counts for v3.1 vs v3.0 over heldout 2.4k paired comparisons):
- Wins (v3.1 better): 1468
- Losses (v3.1 worse): 824
- Ties: 108
- Net wins: +644 (p<0.001)

Regression signal & triage log:
- Regression alerts auto-detected for math suite on 2026-11-04; severity: P2.
- Reproducer: minimal prompt set attached as 'math-regression-reproset-11-04' in Confluence-2314.
- Root cause hypothesis: training curriculum changed the loss weighting for symbolic tokens; model now favors surface heuristics over exact arithmetic encoding.
- Action: patch branch train/fix-symbolic-weights (PR#459) in progress; expected turnaround 72–96 hours.

Decision rationale:
- Why canary? v3.1 brings substantive user-facing quality gains (synthesis, RAG) and cost parity. The regression is localized to a definable prompt family and a queued patch is available. Canary will let us validate real traffic effects and monitor latency jitter in production.
- Why not immediate global rollout? The math regression affects a small but high-value set of routes (billing analytics, internal reporting). Full rollout risks customer-facing inaccuracies.

Canary plan (proposed):
- Phase 0: internal dedicated canary (redwood-internal routes) — 48 hours monitoring with live human audits on math and billing routes. Block if >3% increase in numeric failures.
- Phase 1: 2% of hosted API traffic + dedicated low-traffic clusters for 7 days. Auto-fallback to v3.0 on error rate increase >1% or p95 latency > +20% for 1 hour.
- Phase 2: 10% traffic for 7 days, run golden prompt set daily and rollback on any regression beyond thresholds.

Monitoring & gates (metrics to watch):
- Daily human preference delta sampled on open-ended prompts (n=300).
- Math-suite exact-match rate and delta vs baseline.
- Latency p95 trend, kernel-contention metric, and queue length.
- Hallucination rate on RAG subset.
- Safety flags and PSP (policy) triggers.

Action items (owners):
- Patch symbolic weighting (Ethan Brooks) — PR#459 — ETA 72h.
- Add math-suite golden triggers to CI (Riley Moreno) — deploy by 2026-11-08.
- Canary orchestration + fallback policy config (SRE: Priya Desai) — schedule window 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-25.
- Update model card with known regression and furnished mitigations (Avery Chen) — post canary start.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Acceptable math-suite tolerance for hosted customers — propose QPS-weighted threshold or customer-tier exemptions?
- Should dedicated & private customers get opt-in early access to v3.1 given the RAG/hallucination improvements?

Appendices:
A) Representative diffs from human eval (anonymized):
- Example A (summarization): v3.0 omitted paragraph on regulatory detail; v3.1 correctly preserved and cited.
- Example B (math): v3.0: 24.0; v3.1: 23.6 (incorrect rounding chain).

B) Repro commands & minimal config:
- see linked_artifacts: github.com/redwood-inference/model-registry/pull/452 for infra harness and CONFLUENCE-2314 for prompt sets and raw scores.

C) Full numeric tables are attached to Confluence-2314. Raw human rating CSVs: s3://redwood-evals/variance-nov2026/human_ratings.csv

Notes to reviewers: please focus review on the canary gating thresholds and whether the math-suite block should be applied to any customer-facing route beyond billing. Add comments inline or ping the thread in #applied-ml-evals.
